issues.description: Function make_y_state: the problem statement and the solution define make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (including a depolarization parameter p), but the template defines make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None (missing the p parameter). The template's docstring even documents a p parameter, so the signature/documentation diverge. This mismatch will cause student code and tests (which expect to pass a depolarization probability p) to fail or be confusing.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter so it matches the problem statement and solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the docstring parameter list to match and mention p's purpose (single-qubit depolarizing noise strength).

issues.description: The exercise expects a function make_y_state that prepares a noisy |Y> resource with a depolarization parameter p. Problem statement: declares make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Template repository: the stub is defined as make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None (missing the p parameter). Solution repository: implements make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. This signature mismatch (missing the depolarization parameter in the template) prevents students from matching the API in the problem description and from implementing or calling helper functions (e.g., teleport_s) that pass p through to make_y_state, causing confusion and likely runtime errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template stub to match the problem statement and solution: change the function signature in template/msd.py to def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, and update the docstring to document the depolarization parameter p. Ensure any template example calls or helper functions in the template that should pass p are updated to do so (e.g., teleport_s should pass p to make_y_state).
